summary.headline: Canara Robeco FY26 PAT rose 7% to INR203.8 crores, with revenue from operations up 17% to INR424.9 crores; Q4 costs were inflated by one-offs.
summary.overview: Closing AUM was about INR1.07 lakh crores at March 31, 2026, up about 3.2% YoY, while quarterly average AUM grew 14% YoY to about INR1.17 lakh crores. FY26 revenue from operations rose 17.0% to INR424.9 crores and total income rose 13.0% to INR454.6 crores. Management attributed Q4 other expenses and employee costs partly to one-offs (NFO marketing, labour code, regulatory and technology spend). The call flagged a weak SIP trend over three quarters, which management attributed mainly to mark-to-market and tax-related ELSS changes. Management also said a BER structure replacing TER is still being assessed.

financial_highlights.change: vs 35.5 bps in prior comparison (as stated by analyst)
Equity 37 bps, fixed income 30 bps, liquid 3 bps
down from INR26 crores in Q3 per analyst; management says one-offs included

financial_highlights.value: about INR15.7-16 crores per analyst reference to last quarter
financial_highlights.change: up about 34-35% YoY in Q4 per analyst; FY26 up about 24%

segments.name: Equity-oriented AUM
segments.commentary: Roughly 91% of AUM is equity-oriented; equity yield was about 37 bps in FY26. Management says the fund house underperforms in down markets and outperforms in up markets.

segments.name: Fixed income
segments.commentary: Fixed income yield was about 30 bps in FY26; liquid yield about 3 bps.

segments.name: Investor mix
segments.commentary: Individual investors hold about 86% of AUM and institutions about 14%. Management said SIPs contribute about one-third of AUM.

guidance_outlook: Management expects employee costs to rise from the Q4 level as branches (29 from 23) and regulatory costs grow; cost-to-income target is 40-50%.
Employee cost run-rate going forward is not yet guided; the company will show the new normal from Q1 FY27.
BER replacing TER with GST separate: impact still being evaluated with distributors; at worst neutral, at best a gain of a couple of bps.
Yield comfort range is 32-40 bps; management says PAT is the more important metric.
Another NFO is planned in the next four to five months, pending regulatory approval; about two NFOs a year is the norm, including this financial year.
Dedicated SIP sales teams across five locations; management expects a directional change in SIP book growth within six months.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 29 from 23 a year earlier.
Technology investments made to support regulatory environment were cited as one-off Q4 costs.
Over 56,000 empanelled distribution partners; over 50.8 lakh investor folios.
Company remains active (not passive); index funds, commodity funds and ETFs are not planned in the near term, and AIF/PMS entry is not prioritised.
demand_pricing: Industry Q4 FY26 average AUM about INR81.5 lakh crores, up about 21% YoY but only about 0.7% QoQ; March 2026 SIP inflows above INR32,000 crores (all-time high); industry SIP AUM INR50.1 lakh crores (about 20% of MF assets).
Management said Canara Robeco's flows were in line with or better than industry, but declined to give figures; said market share was roughly maintained.
SIP AUM declined more than overall AUM in Q4; management attributed this to mark-to-market, as equity markets fell about 15%.
B30 AUM declined QoQ, which management attributed to Q4 mark-to-market and said is in line with industry; management said B30 market share was retained.
Digital/direct channel accounts for 28% of AUM.
Management said the industry is commoditised and performance and trust are the differentiators.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue yield rise to 39 bps from 35.5 bps, and what are segment yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is likely due to expensive assets leaving the system and being replaced by cheaper ones; still investigating. FY26 yields: equity 37 bps, fixed income 30 bps, liquid 3 bps, overall about 35 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the TER-to-BER change from April?
qa_highlights.answer: Still being evaluated; the company is discussing with key distributors how to share the impact. Worst case neutral, best case a gain of a couple of bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR23-24 crores a quarterly run-rate for employee costs?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said INR23 crores is the new normal for now, but headcount, increments and income growth will push costs up; CEO said model using cost-to-income of 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply in Q4, and will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 included one-offs: NFO-related advertising and marketing, and regulatory and risk-related costs. Costs will fall slightly but will not return to the Q4 level given higher turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What were the advisory (Onex) fee revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarterly breakup not disclosed; more than 90% of fees come from management fees. The annual report will contain the split.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows and folios decline for three quarters, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO attributed it to macro and tax factors (ELSS changes) and market mark-to-market. Dedicated SIP sales teams across five locations and a digital SIP reactivation campaign launched three days before the call. ELSS is about 8% of equity AUM, not all SIP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company launch ETFs, index funds, NRI or foreign-market funds, or enter PMS/AIF?
qa_highlights.answer: No near-term plans for ETFs, index or commodity funds, or AIFs; focus stays on active mutual funds. Foreign-market and NRI schemes are being looked at as a possibility.

risks_watch: SIP book trend: SIP AUM fell faster than total AUM in Q4, and ELSS tax changes may weigh on flows.
Cost base: Q4 included one-offs; next quarter's employee and other expenses will show the true run-rate.
Yield trajectory: Q4 yield rose to 39 bps, but the reasons are still under review, and equity yield trails some peers.
BER transition: distributor sharing of the impact is still unresolved.
Market-linked AUM: about 91% equity exposure means underperformance in down markets; Q4 Nifty fell about 15%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term franchise and performance, but defensive on Q4 SIP, flow and cost questions, attributing them to mark-to-market and one-offs. Management declined to quantify flows, advisory fees and one-off amounts, and deferred several answers to next quarter.
key_quotes: So, ours is a commoditized business in more ways than one, and your true differentiator will be the trust you're able to build with your investors and performance over time.
For us, we are comfortable with yields being in the range of 32 to 40. That's the range we look at, but we focus more on PAT.
At worst, we will be neutral on this, at best we probably may gain a couple of basis points.

growth.why: No numeric revenue growth guidance; management gives cost-to-income range 40-50% and yield comfort range 32-40 bps, plus about two NFOs a year with one due in 4-5 months, but no sized capacity or orders back growth, while SIP flows have declined for three quarters.
